title: 10 Supermetrics alternatives for marketing data in 2026
summary: Compare 10 Supermetrics alternatives for marketing data pipelines, reporting, and QA, with pricing, limits, and practical selection criteria.
body_markdown:
Most Supermetrics alternatives move marketing data into a dashboard or warehouse. That's useful, but it doesn't prove that a purchase fired once, carried the right value, or included the identifiers an ad platform needs.


The usual advice is to compare connector counts and pick the cheaper subscription. **Start with the job instead.** A data hub standardizes channel data. A connector feeds your existing reports. An agency reporting platform handles client presentation. A monitoring layer checks the conversion signals behind those reports.


The distinction matters when GA4 and Meta disagree. Replacing the connector won't repair a duplicate CAPI purchase. Equally, a tracking audit won't replace a warehouse pipeline that joins campaign spend to CRM revenue.


Evaluate candidates against these requirements:


- **Source coverage:** Test the accounts, fields, and breakdowns your reports use.
- **Destinations:** Confirm that your spreadsheet, BI tool, or warehouse is supported on the intended plan.
- **Pricing model:** Count accounts, clients, destinations, users, and any usage limits.
- **Refresh frequency:** Match delivery to your reporting cadence rather than buying speed you won't use.
- **Validation:** Separate successful extraction from evidence that the underlying conversion is correct.


These Supermetrics alternatives serve different jobs. Choose the category first, then compare the products within it.


## 1. Trackingplan


Trackingplan


**Best for checking whether the conversion data behind reporting can be trusted.** Trackingplan is a digital analytics agent that audits real user traffic on websites, iOS and Android apps, and server-side endpoints, checking every request sent to **more than 170 analytics and ad providers** . A connector moves data. This checks whether the data was right in the first place.


For paid media, it compares signals across the Meta Pixel, the Conversions API, and GA4. It flags purchases counted twice or not at all, incorrect values, weak click-ID and match-rate coverage, and broken UTMs or campaign naming. Each finding links to the underlying hits, so an analyst can open the affected event instead of working backward from dashboard totals.


### Where it fits in the workflow


Describe a report, audit, or conversion check once in plain English. Scheduled automations run **daily or weekly** and deliver results to Slack, Teams, email, or a webhook, while continuous monitoring catches anomalies between runs. Monitoring, alerts, and daily digests are part of the sessions fee, not metered per task.


- **Conversion evidence:** Inspect the event, property, and value behind a discrepancy, verified on real traffic.
- **Implementation monitoring:** Catch changed tracking behavior, missing properties, and dataLayer issues across sites, apps, and server-side.
- **Privacy checks:** Monitor consent and detect PII in tracking payloads.
- **Agency operations:** Reuse recurring checks across client implementations.


It makes sure campaigns are optimized on conversion data the team can trust.


Starter and Growth start with a **9-day free trial** . A practical way to use it: point it at a known GA4-versus-Meta discrepancy and see whether the evidence reaches the person who owns the tag.


## 2. Funnel


Funnel


Funnel suits teams whose analysts repeatedly clean the same channel data before reporting. It combines **collection, preparation, and reporting in a hosted marketing-data hub** . Rules let teams standardize metrics, budgets, campaign dimensions, and business logic before sending data onward.


Funnel lists Starter at **$300/month billed annually** , with **100+ connectors and 13 destinations** , and Business from **$600/month billed annually** , with **600+ connectors and 47 destinations** . A **14-day trial** is available.


The practical advantage is reusable preparation. Say several brands use different campaign naming conventions. An analyst can define mappings centrally rather than maintaining separate spreadsheet formulas for each report.


**What works:** Standardization across brands and channels, built-in dashboards, exports, Funnel AI, and MCP access. It's a sensible step beyond connectors when repeated cleanup has become the main reporting task.


**Where it stops:** Connector and destination availability varies by plan. A team moving a small set of sources into Sheets may not need a hosted hub. Standardized campaign fields also don't prove that the website sent a valid purchase event.


Test the mapping rules with awkward source data, not just a clean demonstration account.


## 3. Windsor.ai


Windsor.ai


If your reporting destination already works, Windsor.ai is worth testing as the replacement data pipe. It connects marketing sources to Looker Studio, Power BI, Google Sheets, BigQuery, and Snowflake without requiring a full marketing-data hub.


Windsor.ai lists **350+ data sources** and a Basic plan at **$19/month billed annually** , covering **three sources and 75 accounts** . Its free plan has narrower ongoing limits than the **30-day trial** , so don't estimate production capacity from the trial workspace.


### Evaluate the source-and-account combination


A source limit and an account limit are different constraints. An agency with many accounts on the same advertising platform has a different requirement from an in-house team using advertising, commerce, CRM, and analytics systems.


- **Strengths:** Broad listed source coverage, warehouse destinations across plans, data blending, and AI/MCP access.
- **Trade-offs:** Limits include sources, accounts, and destination tasks. Basic can become restrictive when the channel mix expands.
- **Boundary:** Moving and blending platform totals doesn't establish why those totals differ.


AI access is useful only when the connected metrics retain their definitions. Before connecting an assistant, review how to[connect AI to marketing data](https://www.trackingplan.com/guides/connect-ai-to-marketing-data) without losing context around attribution, date ranges, and source fields.


Test a campaign-level export with the exact dimensions your dashboard needs. A supported platform name isn't enough.


## 4. Improvado


Improvado


**Improvado is an enterprise pipeline decision, not a lightweight spreadsheet substitution.** It combines marketing ETL, managed mapping, and delivery to analytics workflows across paid media, analytics, CRM, commerce, and other systems.


Improvado lists Starter from **$20,000/year** , Growth from **$41,700/year** , and custom Enterprise pricing; its separate MCP-only product is listed at **$100/month** . Don't compare that MCP subscription with a full pipeline plan.


The case for the platform is managed consistency. A large organization may need common campaign taxonomies and metric definitions across business units before analysts can build useful cross-channel reports. Managed mapping can reduce the need for each analyst to interpret those fields independently.


### Buy the mapping, not just the connector list


**Pros:** Broad marketing integration coverage and managed data mapping.


**Cons:** The main plans require a substantial budget and a sales conversation. Small teams with basic reporting needs may pay for capabilities they won't use.


Ask the evaluation team to demonstrate a difficult join, such as campaign spend connected to qualified CRM outcomes. Inspect unmatched records and mapping exceptions, not only the finished chart.


A prepared data model helps analysts compare channels. It still needs valid identifiers and conversion events at the source.


## 5. Coupler.io


Coupler.io


Say your weekly report combines campaign spend, CRM records, and a spreadsheet maintained by sales. Coupler.io fits that import-and-prepare workflow without requiring a large analytics platform.


[Coupler.io](https://www.coupler.io/) lists **400+ sources** , annual plans at **$24/month for Starter** , **$99/month for Active** , and **$199/month for Pro** , plus a free plan and **seven-day trial** . Starter includes **three accounts and one destination** , so model the actual setup before treating the entry price as your expected bill.


Destinations include Google Sheets, Excel, Looker Studio, Power BI, and warehouses. Data blending, transformations, dashboard templates, and client workspaces support reporting beyond a basic export.


- **What works:** Automated imports and preparation across marketing and business applications.
- **What to inspect:** Connected-account allowances, destinations, transformation requirements, and workspace access.
- **What it won't prove:** Whether a tag fired correctly or a browser purchase was deduplicated against its server-side equivalent.


Keep data pipelines separate from action workflows. The[Zapier workflow automation breakdown](https://fruitpunch.ai/review/zapier) is useful context when deciding whether a task needs structured imports or app-to-app actions.


For the trial, deliberately change a source column or campaign label. Check whether the destination remains usable and whether the failure is visible to the reporting owner.


## 6. Porter Metrics


Porter Metrics


Agencies that already build reports in Looker Studio should evaluate Porter Metrics before adopting a separate reporting environment. It connects advertising, social, analytics, and commerce sources to reporting destinations and supports reusable client dashboards.


[Porter Metrics](https://portermetrics.com/) starts at **$15/month for one account** , with volume discounts, unlimited users and reports on reporting subscriptions, and a **14-day trial** followed by a free plan. Standard paid Reporting plans exclude BigQuery, which is available on Enterprise.


### Count connected accounts before comparing costs


Per-account pricing can be straightforward, but an agency needs to inventory every billable connection. A client relationship isn't necessarily the same unit as a connected account.


**Useful capabilities** include data blending, custom fields, white-label dashboards, and delivery to Looker Studio, Sheets, Power BI, and AI/MCP tools. These suit agencies that want to keep their existing report-building process.


**The trade-off** is that the analyst still owns the report model and its definitions. A connector doesn't monitor purchase quality because it exports conversions successfully.


Use the[SEM reporting tools guide](https://www.trackingplan.com/blog/sem-reporting-tools) to distinguish presentation needs from data preparation and tracking checks. During evaluation, build a reusable dashboard with client-specific filters and confirm that copied reports don't retain another client's account selection.


That operational detail matters more than an attractive template when an agency scales reporting across its portfolio.


## 7. Dataslayer


Dataslayer


**Migration effort can outweigh subscription savings.** Dataslayer deserves attention when a team likes its existing Supermetrics workflow and wants to preserve spreadsheet queries or BI reports rather than rebuild the reporting stack.


[Dataslayer](https://www.dataslayer.ai/) lists annual Starter, Advanced, and Pro plans at **€29/month, €99/month, and €299/month** , respectively, alongside a free plan and **15-day trial** . Starter allows **three connectors** , paid plans include unlimited users, and the plans list importing data from Supermetrics.


The product connects sources such as Google Ads, Meta Ads, GA4, LinkedIn Ads, and TikTok Ads to Looker Studio, Sheets, Excel, Power BI, and warehouses. Higher plans add blending and AI/MCP features.


- **Migration advantage:** Importing existing queries can reduce rebuild work.
- **Capacity constraint:** Lower paid plans have monthly row limits for warehouse destinations.
- **Evaluation risk:** A successful import doesn't guarantee identical field definitions, filters, or date behavior.


Treat query migration as a starting point. Compare output columns, calculated fields, currency, timezone, and campaign breakdowns before replacing the production connection.


Also test a query with no results and a source authorization failure. The analyst needs to distinguish a genuine zero from an extraction problem.


Dataslayer is most relevant when the reporting workflow is already right. It isn't a reason to keep a fragile spreadsheet model that needs redesign.


## 8. Whatagraph


Whatagraph


Whatagraph puts **client-facing reporting** at the center of the product. Choose it when the main task is aggregating channel data into recurring, branded reports, rather than feeding an independently managed BI environment.


Whatagraph lists Max from **€699/month billed annually** , with **50 or more source credits** , custom branding, goals, alerts, and unlimited users and reports; Prime pricing is custom. Source-credit consumption needs careful evaluation for multi-location businesses and agencies.


### Pay for the reporting workflow you'll use


The appeal is a shared environment for aggregation, templates, transformations, and presentation. A reporting lead can standardize layouts and reduce the need to maintain separate presentation files.


**Pros:** Reporting and branding are central features. Goals and alerts can support recurring client reviews, while templates help teams maintain consistent presentation.


**Cons:** The subscription may be difficult to justify for a smaller agency. Source credits also mean that the visible plan price isn't enough to estimate fit.


Give an account manager the report builder and a real client brief. Evaluate the editing workflow, not just the sample dashboard.


Check how the report explains conversions from different platforms. If a combined total includes different attribution rules, label it clearly rather than presenting it as deduplicated revenue.


Reporting alerts are useful prompts to investigate. They aren't evidence that the underlying Meta Pixel, CAPI, or GA4 implementation is healthy.


## 9. AgencyAnalytics


AgencyAnalytics


An agency may not need another ETL platform. It may need a place where clients can open branded dashboards and receive consistent reports without asking an analyst for exports.


[AgencyAnalytics](https://agencyanalytics.com/) organizes reporting around client accounts, with a Core offer listed at **$20 per client per month, billed annually** and a **14-day trial** . Its integrations span PPC, SEO, social, and other marketing categories.


Client portals, white-label reports, custom dashboards, and automated delivery make the product a candidate for replacing a connector-plus-reporting workflow. Per-client billing also gives account managers a recognizable unit for cost planning.


- **Strong fit:** Agencies prioritizing client access, branded presentation, and repeatable delivery.
- **Main trade-off:** Costs increase with the client roster.
- **Wrong expectation:** Treating it as a flexible warehouse pipeline for complex transformations and cross-channel models.


Use the[client reporting guide](https://www.trackingplan.com/blog/client-reporting) to define what clients need to understand, not just what the integrations can display. A useful report separates performance commentary from unresolved measurement issues.


During the trial, test permissions with a client-style user. Confirm that the account manager can prepare an update without exposing unrelated workspaces or editing the underlying metric definitions.


Choose AgencyAnalytics for the client delivery process. Choose a data hub when the harder problem is preparing and joining the data before anyone sees it.


## 10. Power My Analytics


Power My Analytics


Power My Analytics combines data collection with **managed warehouse storage** . That makes it relevant when a team wants historical data retained without taking responsibility for its own warehouse infrastructure.


[Power My Analytics](https://www.powermyanalytics.com/) lists **85+ sources** and paid plans from **$41.63/month billed annually** , with a **14-day trial without a credit card** .


Sources cover advertising, analytics, social, commerce, email, and CRM systems. Destinations include Looker Studio, Sheets, Excel, Power BI, and warehouses, with MCP access for AI tools.


### Separate storage value from connector value


**Advantages:** The vendor says every plan provides access to all connectors, while paid plans include warehouse storage and data backfill. That can simplify procurement for a team that wants collection and retained history together.


**Limitations:** The free Sample Data plan doesn't connect your own sources. Teams that only need a connector may not need the included warehouse.


Test historical coverage using the fields your report requires. Stored data is useful only if the retained grain supports later questions about campaigns, products, or conversion actions.


Managed storage also doesn't correct a missing transaction identifier. It preserves the records received, so source-event quality still needs separate attention.

A connector can move data on schedule and still leave a broken conversion signal invisible. The destinations column draws the sharpest line. Most rows write into Looker Studio, Sheets, or a warehouse, while the monitoring row sends findings to the tools where a team already works. The two rows without a listed trial also carry enterprise pricing, so plan for a sales conversation rather than a self-serve signup.


## How to choose, and how to keep the data honest


Match the tool to the job before comparing prices.


Choose **Funnel or Improvado** when the job is standardizing marketing data for enterprise reporting or warehouse workflows. Shortlist **Windsor.ai, Coupler.io, or Dataslayer** when a small team mainly needs reliable imports into its existing reporting tools. Look at **Porter Metrics, Whatagraph, or AgencyAnalytics** for client-facing reporting, and **Power My Analytics** when managed historical storage matters.


Then assess the job none of them do. A connector moves fields from a platform to a dashboard and will faithfully deliver a duplicated purchase event or a stripped click ID. Trackingplan covers that gap: it audits real user traffic around the clock across more than 170 analytics and ad providers, checks every event, property and value, and alerts the team when a conversion stops firing or a UTM convention breaks. Run its trial alongside your connector shortlist. The result is campaigns optimized on conversion data the team can trust. Keep the reporting and monitoring decisions separate, even when both feed the same dashboard.


### Explain discrepancies before correcting totals


GA4, Google Ads, and Meta will not produce identical totals, and chasing a single number wastes analyst hours. Differences reflect attribution windows, counting rules, reporting dates, consent, or modeled conversions, as the[TAGGRS discrepancy guide](https://taggrs.io/meta-ga4-and-google-ads-conversions-dont-match/) explains.


Classify each gap as **expected, delayed, modeled, or broken** . Then gather evidence for that classification instead of adjusting formulas until the dashboard looks consistent.


- **Matching problems.**[Meta's verification documentation](https://developers.secure.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/conversions-api/verifying-setup) scores Event Match Quality on a **1-to-10 scale** and typically recommends aiming for **at least 6.0** . Inspect customer-information fields and Pixel/Conversions API deduplication evidence alongside the score.
- **Import delays.**[Google's offline conversion guidance](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1722022) says imports can take **24–48 hours** to process and the attached GCLID must be within **90 days** . Check upload configuration and conversion-action names before diagnosing data loss.
- **Enhanced conversions.**[Google's diagnostics documentation](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/11954870?hl=en) says the diagnostics report can take **up to 48 hours** to show a status after it receives data. Coverage and matching are separate checks.
- **Consent behavior.**[Google's Consent Mode documentation](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/13802165?hl=en) distinguishes storage, personalization, and user-data signals. Inspect what the website and server-side tags send. A visible banner is not evidence.


Pick **two candidates** and run each against a real dashboard. Use the same accounts, date ranges, dimensions, and conversion definitions. Then break things on purpose: drop a record, revoke an authorization, rename a campaign.


Judge the connector on usable reporting output and the monitor on whether each alert gives the responsible owner enough detail to act. The winning setup helps an analyst explain a discrepancy instead of reconciling totals by hand.
